newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Carpenter says PNG reports incorrect.
newsitem.headline: Carpenter says PNG reports incorrect.

text.p: Carpenter Pacific Resources NL, a partner in the Mt Kare gold prospect in Papua New Guinea, said it had sought a trading halt in its shares earlier on Thursday due to various reports which could send its share price lower.

The company said it had been told that certain parties which it did not identify had been offering participation in 30 million Carpenter shares at a substantial discount. The shares were owned by an estate and its executives had advised the company that the parties had no authority to offer the stock.
Carpenter also said the PNG government did not have the ability to suspend its mining licence at Mt Kare, contrary to a report in the Austrlaian Financial Review newspaper.
The company said it had legal advice that the government could not take this action.
Mt Kare is about 17 kilometres southwest of the giant Porgera gold mine in the PNG Highlands.
Carpenter recently said Mt Kare had the potential to match Porgera, which produces about one million ounces of gold each year.

Carpenter's Matu Mining Pty Ltd subsidiary holds the Mt Kare licence. Carpenter is about 33 percent owned by Oakland Pty Ltd, itself 73.2 percent owned by Ramsgate Resources NL which also sought a trading halt on its shares earlier on Thursday.
Canada's Madison Enterprises Corp has an agreement to take a 65 percent stake in Mt Kare once it spends A$10 million.
